S1_incident_reporting.quote: A manufacturer must report any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the competent regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary incident record. It must submit a follow-up report within 10 calendar days, including known circumstances, model and serial number, injuries or damage, and corrective actions. Incidents presenting an ongoing risk must be reported to affected customers and nearby occupants who may be exposed within 48 hours of awareness, with immediate protective instructions. Other affected customers must be notified within 5 calendar days.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a regulator-approved 55 °C sustained-heat test before sale and at least annually, using a consistent protocol and independent accredited laboratory. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% of tested units per model. If a model exceeds 5%, the regulator must require corrective action and a confirmatory test. Pending confirmation, the regulator may authorize continued or limited sales subject to proportionate safeguards, monitoring, and customer notice where warranted by the evidence; it may restrict sales when necessary to address a serious risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units must include a remotely operable emergency shut-off, with secure operation available to the customer and authorized emergency responders. For units already installed when this rule takes effect, manufacturers must provide a no-cost retrofit or equivalent compliant upgrade within six years.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. The suppression system must be designed and validated for the unit’s battery chemistry and foreseeable operating conditions, and must not create an unreasonable risk of toxic exposure or impede emergency response.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a regulator-supervised recall when a model’s thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. The manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop new sales, and provide repair, replacement, or refund options and safe handling instructions.

document.section_notes: S1 is strong: all incidents reportable within 24h, customer notice within 48h/5d, and no withholding during investigation. S2 sets a 5% limit at 55°C with per-model results to customers and regulators but no public per-model rates, yet it lets the regulator authorize continued sales above the limit pending corrective action. S3 requires new-unit shut-off and a 6-year retrofit; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8/100k with prompt notices but no explicit serious-injury clause.
